listening_material_parts.scenario: A volunteer speaks to a community project coordinator about registering for a local environmental clean-up project.

turns.speaker: speaker1
turns.text: This is the IELTS Listening test. You will hear four different recordings, and there are questions on what you hear. You will have time to read the questions before you listen, and you will have time to check your answers after each part. Listen carefully, because you will hear each recording once only. The test has four parts. At the end of the test, you will be given ten minutes to transfer your answers to an answer sheet. Now turn to Part 1. You will hear a volunteer speaking to a coordinator at a community centre about joining a local environmental project. First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 5. You should answer the questions as you listen, using the information given in the recording.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Good morning, Greenbank Community Centre. This is the environmental projects desk. How can I help?

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Hello. I'd like to register for one of your weekend clean-up projects, if there are still places available.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Certainly. I can take some details and explain how the project works. May I start with your name?

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Yes, it's Anna Moreno. I've recently moved to the area and would like to meet other local volunteers.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Thank you. Your surname is spelt M-O-R-E-N-O.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: That's right, Moreno. Please use my personal email address when you send the project information.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Of course. Have you done any organised volunteering before, or will this be your first community activity?

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: This will be my first organised project, although I often collect rubbish when I walk my dog near the park.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: That's useful experience. The first thing people usually ask about is where everybody meets.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: The meeting point is the east entrance of Riverside Park, beside the large noticeboard.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Fine. And when is the next clean-up taking place? I need to put it in my calendar.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: The next session is on Saturday 14 June, and volunteers should arrive a few minutes before the start.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Saturday 14 June is suitable for me. I don't have any other plans that morning.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Good. You may also be wondering what you need to bring with you on the day.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: We provide litter pickers and gloves for every volunteer, so the basic equipment is ready when you arrive.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: That sounds helpful. The former will be especially useful for reaching things near the edge of the path.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Exactly. Our team checks all the equipment before the session, and someone will show new volunteers how to use it safely.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: There is one age rule that I should mention before I complete the first part of your registration.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: The minimum age is 16, although younger children can come with a parent for other community events.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: I'm over 16, so that requirement is fine. Thank you for explaining it clearly.

turns.speaker: speaker1
turns.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 6 to 10. Please read the questions carefully and think about the kind of information you need to listen for.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Could you tell me how long the clean-up lasts? I am planning my travel home afterwards.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: It was originally planned for three hours, but it has been reduced to two and a half hours in total.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Two and a half hours is manageable. I live nearby, so getting home afterwards should be easy.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: We also divide volunteers between two areas, depending on what sort of work they prefer.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: You can choose the river path or the community garden. The river path usually involves walking, while the garden work is mostly in one place.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: I'd prefer the river path, please. I enjoy being outdoors and walking while I work.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: I'll note that preference. On the day, the group leader will introduce everyone before you begin.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Another practical point is refreshments during the break. Would you like to know what we offer?

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: We provide tea and coffee at the community centre after the clean-up, along with some simple biscuits.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: That's very kind. I'll bring a bottle of water with me as well, especially if the weather is warm.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Now I need to give you the code for your registration, which you should keep for your records.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: The registration code is ECO-47B, written E-C-O, four-seven-B.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: I've written ECO-47B down. Is there anything else I should remember before I come?

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Just one final safety requirement about clothing, since the work can involve uneven ground and small pieces of glass.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Please wear closed shoes with a firm sole for the session.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: All right, I have suitable walking shoes. Thanks for taking me through all the arrangements.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: You're very welcome. We look forward to seeing you at Riverside Park on the day.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Thank you. Goodbye.

turns.speaker: speaker1
turns.text: That is the end of Part 1. You now have half a minute to check your answers for this part. You will now turn to Part 2.

listening_material_parts.scenario: A learner contacts a local driving school to arrange driving lessons and ask about prices, an instructor, and suitable lesson times.

turns.speaker: speaker1
turns.text: This is the IELTS Listening test. You will hear four different recordings, and you will have to answer questions on what you hear. There will be time for you to read the questions, and you will have the opportunity to check your answers. You should answer as you listen, because the recording will not be played again. You will hear each recording once only. The test has four parts. At the end of the test, you will be given ten minutes to transfer your answers to an answer sheet. Now turn to Part 1. For Questions 1 to 5, listen to a learner who is enquiring about driving lessons at a local school. First you have some time to look at Questions 1 to 5.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Good morning, Greenway Driving School. How can I help you today?

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Hello. I'm hoping to start lessons soon, and I'd like to find out how your school works before I book anything.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Of course. We provide regular lessons for new learners, and I can explain the prices, instructors, and available times.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: That would be helpful. I'm still deciding what kind of car I would feel most comfortable learning in.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: We teach in both manual and automatic cars, but many beginners choose automatic because they can focus on the road.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: The latter sounds better for me, as I have never driven before and want to build confidence gradually.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: An individual lesson is $48. Actually, the current rate is $45 per hour, following our recent price update.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Right, so it is $45 for each hourly lesson. That seems manageable if I begin with one lesson a week.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: We also have a ten-lesson package, and the total price for that package is $420.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: I may choose the package once I know whether the instructor's teaching style suits me.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: For planning ahead, the fee for using our car on the practical driving test is $65.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Thank you. I wanted to include that $65 test fee in my budget from the beginning.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: The instructor who usually teaches new automatic learners is Helen Morrow — that's M-O-R-R-O-W.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Helen Morrow, M-O-R-R-O-W. I'll write that down, because I may need to contact her directly later.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: She is very patient with first-time learners and usually explains each new skill clearly before you practise it.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: That sounds encouraging. My main concern now is finding a regular evening time after work.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: We can certainly look at the evening timetable and find a suitable place for you to meet the instructor.

turns.speaker: speaker1
turns.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at Questions 6 to 10. Now listen carefully and answer Questions 6 to 10.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: I finish work at five thirty, so I would prefer a lesson on a weekday evening rather than during the day.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: We have evening spaces on Tuesday or Thursday. Both are taught by Helen and follow the same usual lesson plan.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Tuesday is best for me, because my work meetings are normally finished by then and I can arrive without rushing.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Fine. There is a regular Tuesday slot available, and I can reserve it when you are ready to enrol.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: The Tuesday lesson starts at 6:15 in the evening, which gives most people time to travel from work.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Six fifteen is ideal. I can get there comfortably after I have changed out of my work clothes.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Each booking lasts 90 minutes, including a short discussion at the beginning about what you will practise that day.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: That seems like enough time to practise properly and still receive some useful feedback before the lesson ends.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: For your first meeting, please wait outside 14 Linden Road, beside the small supermarket entrance.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: I'll meet Helen outside 14 Linden Road. That location is only a short walk from the bus stop.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Please bring your provisional licence to the first lesson, as Helen needs to check it before you drive.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Yes, I already have my provisional licence, so I will keep it with my other documents for Tuesday.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: When you decide to book, you can call this number again, and our office staff will arrange the first lesson.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Great. I'll check my diary this evening and call back soon to reserve the Tuesday time.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: You're welcome. We look forward to helping you get started with your driving lessons.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Thank you very much for all your help. Goodbye.

turns.speaker: speaker1
turns.text: That is the end of Part 1. You now have half a minute to check your answers. You will now turn to Part 2.
